---
title: "Luzon - Rice: from the plain to the terraces"
nocite: |
  @faostat_qcl
subtitle: "The same flooded rice, planted from the lowlands of northern Luzon up into the Cordillera, 33 years, two seasons: what changes with height is temperature, and the model shows where heat and where cold take their share"
---

```{ojs}
import {withDownload, cellFeatures, fmt, locatorMap, placeMarks, boxPolygon, maskTable, maskLabels} from "../assets/js/dl.js"
S = FileAttachment("data/luzon/summary.json").json()
B = FileAttachment("data/luzon/boundaries.json").json()
countries = FileAttachment("data/luzon/countries.geojson").json()
adm1 = FileAttachment("data/luzon/adm1.geojson").json()
adm2 = FileAttachment("data/luzon/adm2.geojson").json()
cells = FileAttachment("data/luzon/cells.csv").csv({typed: true})
bands = FileAttachment("data/luzon/bands.csv").csv({typed: true})
years = FileAttachment("data/luzon/years.csv").csv({typed: true})
SEASON = ({wet: "wet season (transplanted 1 July)", dry: "dry season (transplanted 1 December)"})
LOSS = ({domain: ["lost to heat", "lost to cold"], range: ["#d1495b", "#3c6fb4"]})
canopyTmin = t => (t - 0.87) / 0.92          // Tmin at which the canopy (0.87 + 0.92 Tmin) reaches t
```

| Setup | |
|---|---|
| Area | 120.5-121.5 E, 16.0-17.0 N, northern Luzon, from the plain into the Cordillera (regions and provinces below) |
| Crop map | MapSPAM 2020 rice, physical area [@spam2020] |
| Weather, soil, height | AgERA5 1990-2024 [@agera5]; SoilGrids 2.0 [@poggio2021], one profile per 0.1° cell; elevation: ETOPO1 [@amante2009], mean over each 0.1° cell |
| Crop, template | CERES-Rice, IR 64 (DSSAT cultivar IB0015) and IR 58 (IB0012), 105 kg N/ha; template `XDRI8601.RIX`, from the IRRI experiment IRMZ8601 (Muñoz, 1986); flooded everywhere, so water plays no part |
| Seasons | wet: transplanted on 1 July; dry: transplanted on 1 December; every year |
| Scenarios | the baseline; the same without cold sterility (TCLDF 0); the same without heat sterility (THOT 45). The grain each stress costs is the difference with the baseline, season by season |
| Years | 1991-2023 |
| Boundaries | edge-matched OCHA administrative boundaries (COD-AB) from HDX: [Philippines](https://data.humdata.org/dataset/cod-ab-phl) (NAMRIA, PSA), CC BY-IGO |
| Experiment file | [`configs/cases/luzon-rice.yml`](https://github.com/bennyistanto/xdssat/blob/main/configs/cases/luzon-rice.yml) |

## Where

```{ojs}
md`The study box sits in the north of Luzon, in the Philippines.
${B.box_adm1.map((u, i) => `${u.name}${i === 0 ? " takes" : ""} ${fmt.pct(u.share_of_box)}${i === 0 ? " of it" : ""}${
  u.share_of_unit_in_box >= 0.9 ? ` (nearly all of ${u.name} lies inside)` : ""}`).join(", ")}. Rice grows on
${fmt.int(S.ha)} ha of it (MapSPAM 2020), in ${S.cells} of the 0.1° weather cells. The 0.1° cells average the
terrain: their mean heights run from ${fmt.int(S.elev_range[0])} to ${fmt.int(S.elev_range[1])} m, and single fields
inside a mountain cell lie higher or lower than that.`
```

```{ojs}
viewof whereMetric = Inputs.radio(new Map([["Height of the cell", "elev"], ["Crop area in the cell", "area"]]), {value: "elev", label: "Map"})
viewof mask = Inputs.radio(new Map([["MapSPAM 2020 rice (the runs' crop mask)", "ha"], ["LGRIP30 cropland", "ha_lgrip_all"],
  ["LGRIP30 irrigated cropland", "ha_lgrip_irr"]]), {value: "ha", label: "Crop map"})
```

```{ojs}
place = cells.filter(d => d.cultivar === "IR 64" && d.season === "wet")
html`<div class="map-pair">
  ${withDownload(locatorMap(Plot, countries, B, {width: 280, height: 280}), "luzon_locator", "red: the study box")}
  ${withDownload(Plot.plot({
    width: 420, height: 420,
    projection: {type: "equirectangular", domain: boxPolygon([B.box[0] - 0.05, B.box[1] - 0.05, B.box[2] + 0.05, B.box[3] + 0.05])},
    color: whereMetric === "elev" ? {scheme: "YlOrBr", domain: [0, d3.max(place, d => d.elev)], legend: true, label: "Mean height of the cell (m, ETOPO1)"}
                                  : {scheme: "YlGn", legend: true, label: `${maskLabels("MapSPAM 2020 rice")[mask]} in the cell (ha)`},
    marks: [
      Plot.geo(cellFeatures(place), {fill: d => d.properties[whereMetric === "elev" ? "elev" : mask], stroke: "white", strokeWidth: 0.3}),
      ...placeMarks(Plot, adm1, adm2, {labels: "adm2"}),
      Plot.geo(boxPolygon(B.box), {stroke: "#d0021b", strokeWidth: 1.5, fill: "none"}),
      Plot.tip(place, Plot.pointer({x: "lon", y: "lat",
        title: d => `${d.lat.toFixed(2)} N, ${d.lon.toFixed(2)} E\nheight ${fmt.int(d.elev)} m\nMapSPAM rice ${fmt.int(d.ha)} ha\n` +
          `LGRIP30 cropland ${fmt.int(d.ha_lgrip_all)} ha, irrigated ${fmt.int(d.ha_lgrip_irr)} ha`})),
      Plot.frame({stroke: "#bbb"})
    ]
  }), `luzon_place_${whereMetric}_${mask}`, "0.1° cells; bold: regions, thin: provinces")}
</div>`
```

```{ojs}
dry64 = new Map(cells.filter(d => d.cultivar === "IR 64" && d.season === "dry").map(d => [`${d.iy}_${d.ix}`, d]))
mt = maskTable(place.map(d => ({...d, dry: dry64.get(`${d.iy}_${d.ix}`)})), "MapSPAM 2020 rice", [
  {label: "Area above 800 m (share)", value: d => d.elev > 800 ? 1 : 0},
  {label: "IR 64 wet season (kg/ha)", value: d => d.hw},
  {label: "IR 64 dry season (kg/ha)", value: d => d.dry?.hw},
  {label: "Heat loss, wet, below 300 m (kg/ha)", value: d => d.elev < 300 ? d.heat_loss : NaN},
  {label: "Cold loss, dry, above 1,200 m (kg/ha)", value: d => d.elev > 1200 ? d.dry?.cold_loss : NaN}], mask)
Inputs.table(mt, {format: {"Area in the cells (ha)": fmt.int, "Correlation with MapSPAM, per cell": fmt.d2,
  "Area above 800 m (share)": fmt.pct, "IR 64 wet season (kg/ha)": fmt.int, "IR 64 dry season (kg/ha)": fmt.int,
  "Heat loss, wet, below 300 m (kg/ha)": fmt.int, "Cold loss, dry, above 1,200 m (kg/ha)": fmt.int}, layout: "auto"})
```

```{ojs}
md`The "Crop map" switch sets the crop area behind the second map and the table: MapSPAM 2020 rice, the runs'
own crop mask, or LGRIP30 cropland, all or irrigated only, for comparison. LGRIP30 counts every cropland pixel,
of any crop, so its area is ${fmt.d1(mt[1]["Area in the cells (ha)"] / mt[0]["Area in the cells (ha)"])} times MapSPAM's rice area, and it
puts ${fmt.pct(mt[1]["Area above 800 m (share)"])} of it above 800 m, against ${fmt.pct(mt[0]["Area above 800 m (share)"])} for MapSPAM. Every
average weights each 0.1° cell by the crop area inside it, not by the area of the cell; the simulated cells,
their yields and the other charts on this page keep the MapSPAM weights. A different map would also change the
soil profiles, which xdssat samples under the crop pixels; LGRIP30 is a single year (nominal 2015).`
```

## Up the slope, the crop slows down

The switches below set the cultivar and the season for every chart on the page.

```{ojs}
viewof cv = Inputs.radio(["IR 64", "IR 58"], {value: "IR 64", label: "Cultivar"})
viewof season = Inputs.radio(new Map([["Wet season (1 July)", "wet"], ["Dry season (1 December)", "dry"]]), {value: "wet", label: "Season"})
```

```{ojs}
sel = cells.filter(d => d.cultivar === cv && d.season === season)
zoneOf = e => e < 300 ? "lowland" : e > 800 ? "highland" : "middle"
zoneMean = (rows, z, k) => { const r = rows.filter(d => zoneOf(d.elev) === z); return d3.sum(r, d => d[k] * d.ha) / d3.sum(r, d => d.ha) }
md`Every cell grows the same ${cv}, flooded and fertilised alike. In the ${SEASON[season]}, a crop below 300 m yields
**${fmt.int(zoneMean(sel, "lowland", "hw"))} kg/ha** and needs **${fmt.int(zoneMean(sel, "lowland", "days"))} days** from
transplanting to maturity; above 800 m it yields **${fmt.int(zoneMean(sel, "highland", "hw"))} kg/ha** in
**${fmt.int(zoneMean(sel, "highland", "days"))} days**. Cooler air slows the crop down, and in this model a longer
season means more time to fill grain. FAOSTAT puts the Philippines' national rice yield at 3.97-4.09 t/ha in
2018-2020 (<a href="#ref-faostat_qcl">FAO 2025</a>): the model's levels are higher; the slope is the result.`
```

```{ojs}
wetCv = cells.filter(d => d.cultivar === cv && d.season === "wet")
tooLong = wetCv.filter(d => d.days > 153)
longShare = d3.sum(tooLong, d => d.ha) / d3.sum(wetCv, d => d.ha)
md`The longer season has a price the yield does not show. From 1 July to 1 December is 153 days. ${tooLong.length === 0 ?
`A wet-season ${cv} crop is harvested within that everywhere in the box.` :
`A wet-season ${cv} crop outlasts that on **${longShare < 0.01 ? "under 1%" : fmt.pct(longShare)}** of the rice area, in
${tooLong.length} cell${tooLong.length > 1 ? "s" : ""} all above **${fmt.int(d3.min(tooLong, d => d.elev))} m**: there the wet crop is
still standing when the dry one is due, and the two seasons of this experiment do not fit in one year. The model runs
each season on its own, so it does not notice.`} Switch the cultivar to compare: IR 58 is the quicker of the two.`
```

```{ojs}
withDownload(Plot.plot({
  height: 320, marginLeft: 60, marginRight: 60,
  x: {label: "Mean height of the cell (m)", grid: true},
  y: {label: "Grain yield (kg/ha, mean of 33 seasons)", grid: true},
  r: {range: [2, 10], label: "rice ha"},
  color: {type: "linear", scheme: "Turbo", legend: true, label: "Days from transplanting to maturity"},
  marks: [
    Plot.dot(sel, {x: "elev", y: "hw", r: "ha", fill: "days", stroke: "white", strokeWidth: 0.5, tip: true,
      title: d => `${d.lat.toFixed(2)} N, ${d.lon.toFixed(2)} E, ${fmt.int(d.elev)} m\n${fmt.int(d.hw)} kg/ha in ${fmt.int(d.days)} days\n` +
        `lost to cold ${fmt.int(d.cold_loss)}, to heat ${fmt.int(d.heat_loss)} kg/ha\nrice ${fmt.int(d.ha)} ha`}),
    Plot.linearRegressionY(sel, {x: "elev", y: "hw", stroke: "#555", strokeDasharray: "4,3"})
  ]
}), `luzon_yield_by_height_${season}`, "one dot per 0.1° cell, its size the rice area; dashed: linear fit")
```

## Heat at the bottom, cold at the top

```{ojs}
md`In CERES-Rice a crop loses grains when the days before heading are too hot or too cold. The model watches those days
(\`RI_Phenol.for\`, DSSAT-CSM 4.8). It counts the cold as the degrees by which the canopy, estimated as 0.87 + 0.92 × the
night minimum, falls below the cultivar's **TCLDF**: 15 °C for both cultivars, so nights colder than
${fmt.d1(canopyTmin(15))} °C count. It counts the heat when the mean of 0.75 × Tmax + 0.25 × Tmin over those days
passes **THOT**: ${fmt.d1(S.coefficients[cv].THOT)} °C for ${cv}, each degree above it costing a tenth of the grains. The
grain number takes the worse of the two (\`RI_Grosub.for:409\`). In the two weeks before flowering, lowland cells
average a minimum of **${fmt.d1(zoneMean(sel, "lowland", "tmin14"))} °C** and a maximum of
**${fmt.d1(zoneMean(sel, "lowland", "tmax14"))} °C**; highland cells **${fmt.d1(zoneMean(sel, "highland", "tmin14"))}** and
**${fmt.d1(zoneMean(sel, "highland", "tmax14"))} °C**.`
```

```{ojs}
bandRows = bands.filter(d => d.cultivar === cv && d.season === season)
lossRows = bandRows.flatMap(d => [
  {band: d.band, kind: "lost to heat", kg: d.heat_loss, ha: d.ha, hw: d.hw},
  {band: d.band, kind: "lost to cold", kg: d.cold_loss, ha: d.ha, hw: d.hw}])
withDownload(Plot.plot({
  height: 300, marginLeft: 60,
  x: {label: "Height band of the cell (m)", type: "band", tickFormat: d => `${d}-${d + 200}`},
  y: {label: "Grain lost (kg/ha, mean of 33 seasons)", grid: true},
  color: {legend: true, ...LOSS},
  marks: [
    Plot.barY(lossRows, Plot.stackY({x: "band", y: "kg", fill: "kind", inset: 4, tip: true,
      title: d => `${d.band}-${d.band + 200} m (${fmt.int(d.ha)} ha of rice)\n${d.kind}: ${fmt.int(d.kg)} kg/ha\n` +
        `yield ${fmt.int(d.hw)} kg/ha`})),
    Plot.ruleY([0])
  ]
}), `luzon_losses_by_height_${season}`, "area-weighted; loss = scenario without the stress minus the baseline")
```

```{ojs}
wmeanOf = (rows, k) => d3.sum(rows, d => d[k] * d.ha) / d3.sum(rows, d => d.ha)
cvRows = ["IR 64", "IR 58"].map(c => {
  const wet = cells.filter(d => d.cultivar === c && d.season === "wet" && d.elev < 300)
  const dry = cells.filter(d => d.cultivar === c && d.season === "dry" && d.elev > 1200)
  return {c, heatLow: wmeanOf(wet, "heat_loss"), coldHigh: wmeanOf(dry, "cold_loss"), hwHigh: wmeanOf(dry, "hw"),
          tminHigh: wmeanOf(dry, "tmin14")}
})
md`The two stresses keep to their own ends of the slope and their own seasons. Heat takes its share in the
**wet season below 300 m**: IR 64, with a THOT of 28 °C, loses **${fmt.int(cvRows[0].heatLow)} kg/ha** there; IR 58, at
33.9 °C, loses **${fmt.int(cvRows[1].heatLow)} kg/ha**. Cold takes its share in the **dry season above 1,200 m**, where
the minimum in the two weeks before flowering averages ${fmt.d1(cvRows[0].tminHigh)} °C: **${fmt.int(cvRows[0].coldHigh)}** kg/ha for
IR 64 and **${fmt.int(cvRows[1].coldHigh)} kg/ha** for IR 58, out of about ${fmt.int(cvRows[0].hwHigh)} and
${fmt.int(cvRows[1].hwHigh)}. Both share a TCLDF of 15 °C: DSSAT's default, which the cultivar file recommends changing
only with data from cold environments. Below 1,200 m, cold costs either cultivar little in any season.`
```

## Cold years

```{ojs}
hy = years.filter(d => d.cultivar === cv && d.season === "dry" && d.zone.startsWith("highland"))
ly = years.filter(d => d.cultivar === cv && d.season === "wet" && d.zone.startsWith("lowland"))
worstCold = hy.reduce((a, b) => (b.cold_loss > a.cold_loss ? b : a))
worstHeat = ly.reduce((a, b) => (b.heat_loss > a.heat_loss ? b : a))
md`A mean hides the bad years. Over all rice above 800 m, ${cv}'s dry-season cold loss peaks at
**${fmt.int(worstCold.cold_loss)} kg/ha** in the season of ${worstCold.season_year}-${worstCold.season_year + 1}, when the minimum in the two
weeks before flowering averaged ${fmt.d1(worstCold.tmin14)} °C. ${worstHeat.heat_loss < 1 ?
`Below 300 m, ${cv} loses nothing to heat in any wet season.` :
`Below 300 m, the wet-season heat loss peaks at **${fmt.int(worstHeat.heat_loss)} kg/ha** in ${worstHeat.season_year}, with a mean
maximum of ${fmt.d1(worstHeat.tmax14)} °C before flowering.`} This chart follows the cultivar switch, not the season switch.`
```

```{ojs}
yrRows = [...hy.map(d => ({...d, kind: "lost to cold", kg: d.cold_loss, where: "highland (above 800 m), dry season"})),
          ...ly.map(d => ({...d, kind: "lost to heat", kg: d.heat_loss, where: "lowland (below 300 m), wet season"}))]
withDownload(Plot.plot({
  height: 280, marginLeft: 60,
  x: {label: null, tickFormat: d => String(d), ticks: 8},
  y: {label: "Grain lost (kg/ha)", grid: true},
  color: {legend: true, ...LOSS},
  marks: [
    Plot.line(yrRows, {x: "season_year", y: "kg", stroke: "kind", strokeWidth: 1.8}),
    Plot.dot(yrRows, {x: "season_year", y: "kg", fill: "kind", r: 3, tip: true,
      title: d => `${d.where}, season year ${d.season_year}\n${d.kind}: ${fmt.int(d.kg)} kg/ha\n` +
        `two weeks before flowering: Tmin ${fmt.d1(d.tmin14)} °C, Tmax ${fmt.d1(d.tmax14)} °C`}),
    Plot.ruleY([0])
  ]
}), `luzon_loss_years_${cv.replace(" ", "")}`, "area-weighted over the cells of each zone; dry season: the crop transplanted on 1 December of that year")
```


```{ojs}
        `lost to cold ${fmt.int(d.cold_loss)} (${fmt.pct(d.cold_years)} of seasons over 10%)\nlost to heat ${fmt.int(d.heat_loss)} kg/ha`})),
```

## What this does not say

- **Simulated, not observed.** Why the simulated yields differ from official statistics, in every case study:
  [FAQ](../about/faq.qmd#why-do-the-simulated-yields-differ-from-the-official-statistics).
- **Uncalibrated.** IR 64 and IR 58 run with DSSAT's own coefficients, flooded and at 105 kg N everywhere,
  without pests, diseases or weeds. Their cold thresholds are DSSAT's defaults. Varieties grown in the
  mountains, and their real tolerance of cold, are not in this experiment.
- **Smoothed mountains.** AgERA5 and the cell heights are 0.1° averages. A terrace higher than its cell's
  mean is colder than the model's weather for it.
- **One date per season.** Every cell transplants on 1 July and on 1 December. A crop that takes longer in the
  cold may not leave room for a second one; the model runs each season on its own.
- **Losses are model experiments.** Each loss is the yield without that stress minus the baseline, so it
  shows what the model's sterility rules cost, not a measured loss.

## Run it yourself

```bash
python scripts/prepare_weather.py   --config configs/cases/luzon-rice.yml
python scripts/prepare_crop_mask.py --config configs/cases/luzon-rice.yml
python scripts/prepare_soils.py     --config configs/cases/luzon-rice.yml --aoi luzon_rice
python scripts/run_aoi.py           --config configs/cases/luzon-rice.yml
python docs/scripts/export_cases.py luzon
python docs/scripts/export_boundaries.py luzon
```

The export reads the prepared weather (for the temperatures before flowering) and ETOPO1 for the cell
heights (`etopo180` from [ERDDAP](https://gcoos5.geos.tamu.edu/erddap/griddap/etopo180.html), the copy used
here; set its path in `ETOPO` in `docs/scripts/export_cases.py`).
